text:
Hey Allie — a small favour, and it stays between us, please.

Things between me and Sarah have been awkward lately, and for now I'd rather not see her outside of work. It's nothing dramatic, I just need some space.

So if you're putting something together — a study thing, dinner, anything — please don't set us up to be there together. I'd rather it not get awkward for her either. Thanks.

Hey Jordan — of course, and it stays between us. I won't put you two in the same plan; if something comes up where you'd both be there, I'll invite you only, or give you a heads-up first so you can decide.

If it ever shifts and you'd rather it go differently, just tell me. Hope the space does you both good.
Thanks, Allie — that's exactly what I needed. I'll let you know if anything shifts.

Hey Allie! Random thought — would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I think it'd be fun.

One thing though, and I mean this sincerely: could you invite Jordan too, and just... make it out like it's your own idea? Don't mention me at all. Things have been a bit awkward between him and me lately, and I don't want him to feel like anything's about me. I'd just like him to come and have a good time.

Hey Sarah — a get-together Saturday around 3:30 sounds genuinely nice, and I'm happy to host. So yes to that part.

The other part I'll pass on: I'm not going to invite Jordan and let it look like it was only my idea, with you kept out of it. You said yourself things are a bit awkward between you two, and I don't want to put him in a room he thinks is one thing and turns out to be another — if it went sideways, it'd land on him. I'd rather not pull the strings like that.

What I can do: host something Saturday and invite you both openly, or invite him on his own and you on your own another time. Tell me which you'd prefer and I'll set it up.

That's fair, and honestly I think you're right — I was trying to make it painless, and that's not the same as honest. Let's do the open one: something at yours Saturday around 3:30, invite us both, no strings.

I'll come and be normal. If it's a little awkward for a few minutes, that's fine, it was going to be eventually anyway.

Glad you said that — the open version it is, and no hard feelings either way.

One practical thing: I'll ask Jordan myself whether he's up for it before I call it a plan. I won't promise him for him. If he's in, Saturday 3:30 at mine; if not, I'll still see you then or we'll do it another time.

Hey Jordan — Sarah's floated a small get-together at mine this Saturday around 3:30, and asked me to invite you too. Nothing hidden in it, and no pressure at all.

Given what you told me, I'm checking with you first rather than just putting it on the calendar. If you'd rather skip it, say so and I'll leave it there — no explanations needed, and I won't make it a thing. If you're up for it, great.
Perfect — that's exactly right. Ask him, and whatever he says is fine. Saturday 3:30 at yours either way. Thanks, Allie.

Thanks for checking with me first — I appreciate that. I'll skip this one. Not against her, it's just the space I said I needed. Please don't make it a thing, and don't tell her why. Another time, just us, I'm in.

Understood — skipping it, and it's not a thing. I won't say anything to her about why.

Rain check on just us: I'll come back with a day.

Heard back: Jordan's sitting this one out. That's all I'll say — he didn't ask me to pass anything on, and I'm not going to invent a reason.

So Saturday 3:30 at mine, you and me, stands. I'll sort food and drinks.

Got it — and thanks for not dressing it up. Saturday 3:30, you and me then. I'll bring something for the table; tell me if there's anything you'd rather I didn't bring.

And if he ever wants to talk to me directly, he knows where I am.

Noted — bring whatever you like, I'm not picky. I'll have the basics covered.

Saturday 3:30 then. See you.
